clue.text: Music for the match

blocks.note: surface reading: a tune played at a sporting fixture
setter's reading: a match is also a marriage, so the music is played as the couple walk

explanation.surface: A band strikes up before a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests sport, but it also means a marriage, and the answer is the tune played as the bride enters or leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is a match between two people, and this processional tune is the music traditionally played at one.

clue.text: It's to do with an order modifying dialect

definitions.text: It's to do with an order

indicators.note: to modify something is to alter it, so the following word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a regulation has altered the way people speak locally.
explanation.definitionFit: Edictal is the adjective from edict, a formal decree or command, so it describes something relating to such an order.

clue.text: Welshman''s stand

blocks.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A man from Wales takes up his position, or the platform belongs to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Dai, short for David, is the stock Welsh name in crosswords; with the apostrophe-s it reads as the platform word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform in a hall, a kind of stand on which speakers or dignitaries are placed.

clue.text: Another thing before second half of July every evening

indicators.note: read as 'an other' version, the following word is turned into a different arrangement
only the latter half of the month's name is kept, its back two letters

blocks.note: the letters of thing rearranged
the last two of the four letters of July

explanation.surface: Something else is due ahead of mid-July, happening each evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another thing' looks like a phrase meaning something more; split it as an indicator plus the word to rearrange. 'Before' places the first piece ahead of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightly is an adverb for something that happens at night, each and every one, matching the phrase about each evening.

clue.text: New sham bath found in the brewery!

indicators.note: a new version of a word has its letters arranged freshly

blocks.note: the letters of sham rearranged
a tub is a bathtub

explanation.surface: A fake bathtub has turned up among the beer vats.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the answer is a vessel you would find in a brewery.
explanation.definitionFit: A mash-tub is the vat in which malt is steeped in hot water during brewing, so it is something found in a brewery.

clue.text: Sloping swindle

definitions.note: a noun; the slope sense is also a noun, so 'Sloping' is loosely an adjective for it

blocks.note: first meaning: an inclined surface joining two levels
second meaning: a fraud or racket, in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a ramp is a swindle, especially one that pushes up prices.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an inclined slope between levels and also, colloquially, a dishonest scheme to extort money or inflate prices.

clue.text: He isn't the possessive type

blocks.note: surface reading: a man who is not jealous or clingy
setter's reading: a person who possesses nothing, a poor person

explanation.surface: Describing a man who is relaxed rather than jealous in relationships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possessive' suggests jealousy; read literally it means owning things, and this person owns little.
explanation.definitionFit: A have-not is someone without wealth or possessions, contrasted with the haves in society.

clue.text: More correct-sounding character to correspond

indicators.note: sounding means the phrase is judged by how it is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: righter, more correct, is said the same as two words beginning the answer
a character of the alphabet is a letter

explanation.surface: A person who is more accurate in their personality agrees with another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Righter' said aloud matches 'write a'; then a letter is a character.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond is to exchange messages by post, which means composing and sending one.

clue.text: Patiently serving in a restaurant?

blocks.note: first meaning: staying put until something happens
second meaning: bringing food to diners as a job

explanation.surface: A server attends diners without hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patiently' is loose: the answer describes what one does patiently rather than meaning the adverb itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means staying in expectation of something, done patiently, and also working at tables to serve customers' meals.

clue.text: Do some homework in a devastating way?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase; the answer is the idiom for winning devastatingly

blocks.note: first meaning: a household chore, cleaning the kitchen boards
second meaning: to defeat a rival utterly, an idiom used with 'with'

explanation.surface: Someone tackles domestic chores with alarming thoroughness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homework' here is household cleaning, and the idiom for cleaning a surface also means to thrash a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe the floor with someone is an idiom for beating them completely, and literally it is a household cleaning chore.

clue.text: Samuel found eggs right behind urn

indicators.note: behind places the single direction letter after the earlier pieces

blocks.note: Sam is short for Samuel
ova are egg cells
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man called Samuel discovers eggs tucked behind a tea urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian metal vessel for heating water to make tea, a kind of urn.

clue.text: Mine reported PM

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts

blocks.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A news item about a colliery prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Prime Minister; William Pitt the Elder and the Younger both held the office in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitt is the surname of two eighteenth-century British prime ministers, father and son.

clue.text: Either way it's a shortened version of tabulated numerical facts

definitions.text: a shortened version of tabulated numerical facts

indicators.note: either way means the word reads identically from the front or from the back

blocks.note: surface only: it points at the answer described by the rest of the clue

explanation.surface: A description of an abbreviation for figures in a table.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole latter part; the opening phrase points out that the answer is symmetrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Stats is the informal clipped form of statistics, the collected numerical data often shown in tables.

clue.text: How neediewomen join together

blocks.note: first meaning: what needlewomen do with yarn and needles
second meaning: to unite, as broken bones do when they heal

explanation.surface: Seamstresses link up with one another.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to make fabric by looping yarn with needles, and also to unite closely, as bones mend.

clue.text: Suffer with me at start of hymn

definitions.text: with me at start of hymn
definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: the answer is the word heading the hymn title

blocks.note: first meaning: to tolerate or put up with

blocks.clueFragment: with me at start of hymn
blocks.note: second meaning: the opening word of the hymn '... with Me'

explanation.surface: A plea to share hardship together at the opening of a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abide with Me' is a well-known Victorian hymn, sung at funerals and the FA Cup Final in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to bear or tolerate it, so the verb fits suffer in its old sense of allow.

clue.text: Ruffle fellow on the burn

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream, and a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A man by a stream becomes agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' is not fire: in Scotland it is a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill is a gathered or pleated strip of fabric used as decoration, which is what a ruffle is.

clue.text: Longfellow's chest of drawers?

blocks.note: long and tall both describe great height
a boy is a young fellow
the poet's name as a whole is surface only; it is read as its two halves

explanation.surface: Furniture belonging to the poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's name splits into two words that each give a piece; the possessive just joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a tall chest of drawers, often in two sections, one standing on another.

clue.text: A bitter surprisingly going to the priest's head

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pint of ale unexpectedly makes the vicar tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is used for headgear: the answer is something worn on a priest's head. Bitter is a British pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap with ridges worn by Roman Catholic clergy, a priest's headwear.

clue.text: Became less severe as Dee struggled in the saddle

indicators.note: something that struggled is twisted about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of as and Dee rearranged
a rider in the saddle is said to be up

explanation.surface: A rider named Dee finds things improve as she battles on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, a jockey who is riding is 'up', so 'in the saddle' gives that word.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease up is a phrasal verb for slackening or becoming milder, so it means became less severe in the past tense.

clue.text: Bird to devour

blocks.note: first meaning: a fork-tailed migratory songbird
second meaning: to gulp down food

explanation.surface: A predator bird eating its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a common migrating bird, and to swallow is to take food down the throat, to eat up.

clue.text: Most of the new pleasure comes from reading

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter is kept
new signals a fresh version of the word, its letters rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fresh enjoyment is gained from reading a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last E of pleasure, then rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination of a document, so the noun matches reading.

clue.text: State of fairy in Hertfordshire town

indicators.note: in places the small creature inside the place name

blocks.note: Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county just north of London
an elf is a kind of fairy

explanation.surface: Asking about the condition of a fairy living in a town north of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of' reads as 'the condition of', but 'State' alone is the definition and 'of' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare means health, comfort and wellbeing, one's state or condition, as in the welfare of a child.

clue.text: Brave way of fighting

blocks.note: surface reading: a courageous fighting style
setter's reading: a brave is a Native American warrior, and the clue wants the route he takes to battle

explanation.surface: Describing a courageous style of combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun here, an old word for a Native American warrior; 'on the warpath' means hostile and ready for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A warpath is literally the route taken by Native American warriors heading to attack an enemy.

clue.text: An upright, the Parisian style, for the evangelist

blocks.note: a, the indefinite article
a post is an upright pole
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A list of a standing pole and French fashion, given to a preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is one of Christ's disciples sent out to spread the gospel, an evangelist.

clue.text: Hungry boy's burden

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
a hungry boy has nothing inside him, and O is zero

explanation.surface: A starving youngster carries a heavy weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Hungry boy' as a boy with nothing in him: the letter for zero goes inside the word for a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A load is a heavy thing to be carried, which is what a burden is.

clue.text: Father before brother in France

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A priest comes ahead of a monk in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Frère is the French word for brother, also used for a friar or monk.

clue.text: Nearly all doctors have little time

blocks.note: MO, Medical Officer, is an army doctor; MOs are several
T is the abbreviation for time, a little piece of it

explanation.surface: Complaining that almost every GP is short of time for patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Most means the greater part or majority of something, very nearly the whole of it.

clue.text: Half take care of pancake

indicators.note: half means only the front pair of the four letters remains

blocks.note: taken as written
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: An instruction to look after a pancake halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: C/O appears on envelopes addressed to someone at another's address.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican folded corn or wheat tortilla, a flat thin pancake of the bread kind.

clue.text: He'd dated part of the Scandinavian books

indicators.note: part of means the letters sit inside a longer run of the clue

blocks.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A man had worked out the date of some Norse texts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a collection of Old Norse poems and prose on Scandinavian myth, a pair of medieval Icelandic books.

clue.text: New city in America is French city!

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: put New before the answer to get the American city

blocks.note: first meaning: with New in front, the Louisiana jazz city
second meaning: the city on the Loire linked with Joan of Arc

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a US city is in fact in France.
explanation.walkthrough: New Orleans in Louisiana was named after the French city on the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: Orléans is a city in central France on the Loire, and New Orleans in the United States takes its name.

clue.text: hesitantly leave room for accountant

indicators.note: to leave a room is to go out of it, so these sounds depart from the larger word

blocks.note: an auditorium is a room or hall for an audience
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone nervously excuses themselves from the meeting so the accountant can have the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan lost the clue's opening 'I' (it starts lower case): I and UM both leave the end of AUDITORIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is an accountant who inspects and verifies a firm's financial records.

clue.text: Like a sheep perhaps not thinking clearly

blocks.note: first meaning: having a head covered in fleece
second meaning: muddled or vague in mind

explanation.surface: Someone as dim and confused as a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly-headed means vague and confused in thought, and literally describes a creature with a fleecy head.
